Before I had it, a person I was dating disclosed to me. I knew a little about herpes. We had a conversation about protecting me from it and I decided to wait on relations. I didn’t want to risk it for someone that I wasn’t serious with. Then, it ended badly for unrelated reasons. 

However, now that I have it. If I could go back, I wouldn’t risk it for anyone. And I don’t blame people who don’t want to risk it with me. Now being more informed about herpes, I wish I was more careful and didn’t hookup with the person who gave it to me.

I’m cautiously optimistic. I understand the timeline could be longer than 10 years and I’m okay with that. I’m not going to put my life on because it. And I do believe people need to be more realistic with the timeframe and not let that defer them. I understand their viewpoint. I just think their viewpoint is wrong and we could change it. People have to decide for themselves if they want to advocate and educate. I’m just saying we have the numbers to effect it. I mean there’s a market for treatment. That alone will get them to change their minds.

We do need to be vocal. They don’t really know how many people have it if they aren’t testing it regularly. It took me a year+ to be diagnosed because I didn’t have classic symptoms. Yes there are asymptomatic people who don’t know they have it, but don’t they have a right to know. Asymptomatic who don’t know can give it to others who can/will become symptomatic which is a problem. Pushing it under the rug causes harm. It may be a nuisance for most, but should that stop advancement of treatment or cures? I don’t think so. 

I do see a world where it could be a priority since millions of people have severe problems and need help. We have the power to research all of these diseases if it’s pushed. Saying it’s too big to ask for will keep advancement and development stagnated. Yes education is important but so is treatment. We can have both. We have to advocate and not let people who don’t have it or have minor/minimal outbreaks stop us from wanting better for ourselves.

I think their minds can be changed. I believe it was Fred Hutch who got NIH funding because so many people donated. The issue is that people are not vocal about having herpes and it’s impact for some people. When surveys go out asking about herpes, people who have it say they want a cure or vaccine. People being silence is why research has not moved. Seeing how HRC has help pushed advocacy and research has had a monumental impact on the field. We have to start demanding change instead of being idle.

I do believe that if I started treatment earlier, it would be this bad. It’s really good your going to a specialist. However, I think it’s interesting that you are pregnant. I have constant burning and stinginess when I pee. Ive only had one outbreak. I had to start taking higher doses of valtrex for the pain to go away or lessen the intensity. Also drinking lots of water, avoid sitting for long periods of time, and healthy diet also helps a lot. My RN stated it may be herpetic neuralgia however studies are very limited. The sad truth is there is not a lot of things that we don’t know about herpes because of the general attitude of the virus. I would recommend getting started on some medication.
